# 02 Cement Grind — voicing round (Batch 3A, the fat and driven set)

*Generated by tests/voicing/batch03a.py. Level reading: RMS over the note-on region of the grind riff (phrase j); matched to the bank reference (−18.0 dBFS RMS) by VOLUME; phrase (b)'s reading is in the table too. Every change is before → after under the echo rule. WAVs are on the listen/batch-03a-chapter1-fat-and-driven branch only.*

**Recommended: B centre** — a MONO low-mid grinder: two PULSE oscillators (PW 36 %, 7.8 cents apart) with a triangle LFO on the pulse width at 7.7 Hz (LFO RATE 100) ±15 points deep (LFO PWM 100), restarting with every detached note (LFO PHASE SYNC). Measured on the held A2 the PWM moves the 150-400 Hz band 12.1 dB peak to peak at 7.7 Hz, the 400-1.2k band 7.6 dB, the 3k+ band 7.9 dB and the overall level 4.2 dB; on the riff's 400 ms notes (about 3 swings in each) 7.6 dB in the 150-400 band, 5.4 dB in 400-1.2k, 3.1 dB of level. The original had no PWM at all (its 0.5 Hz filter wobble moved the same band 45 dB, at 0.8 Hz). The filter is a biting 12 dB low-pass (CUTOFF 60, RESO 62) with an envelope decay of 46 ms (FILTER DECAY 58; the first 23 ms of a riff note are 723 Hz against 465 Hz after) and a 12-step glide for the skid; DRIVE 78 before the filter for the crunch (crest 3.2 dB against 6.6 at DRIVE 0). Centroid 527 Hz, 31 % of the energy at 150-400 Hz. Level -18.1 dBFS on the grind riff, -18.4 on phrase (b), peak -14.8, worst case 298 host instr/sample. C is slower (4.6 Hz) and deeper, with narrower pulses and a wider pair (12.5 cents); D is faster (11.6 Hz) with the filter wobbling at the same rate.

## What to listen to

`*_grind.wav` is the one to judge (eight quarter notes with a long gate, a 2.4 s held A2, three short chops): is the PWM obvious on the riff, is it thick, is the filter biting. `*_riff.wav` and `*_stabs.wav` are the pilot phrases (a chord on a MONO patch plays only the last note).
Listen for: the fast sweep of the pulse widths (B at 7.7 Hz against C's slower 4.7 Hz and D's 11.5 Hz with the filter wobbling), the pair's thickness, the drive crunch, the skid at the start of the notes.

*Notes.* The PWM is read on the held A2 (7.2-9.6 s of phrase j) from the energy of five bands in 20 ms frames (depth = 95th minus 5th percentile in dB, rate = strongest component 0.8-20 Hz of that series); the nominal LFO rate is in the table (RATE 100 = 7.7 Hz) and the measured rate matches it.
Deeper or lower-base settings were tried (LFO PWM 127 with PW 34-36: the depth does not grow past about 12 dB in the 150-400 band, and the sweep crosses 50 % so the timbre cycles at twice the LFO rate, 15 Hz): B keeps the sweep one-directional, 21-51 %. The pitch of the pair moves with the VINTAGE offset of card 0 only (MONO).
MONO does not re-fire the envelopes on legato (the riff is detached; LFO PHASE SYNC restarts the PWM with each detached note). Variant A is rendered through the base program path.
